title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 2 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Melton (foot) and Will Johnson (neck) left the Seattle loss with unclear status; Brissett's passing game struggled under pressure and LaFleur wants to review the tape before the next game.
summary: LaFleur called the loss a weird, tough one and said the team was in control in the first half, leading 7-7 at halftime, but the second half fell apart with a string of three-and-outs and six-and-outs. He blamed self-inflicted execution issues and said the team failed to do the ordinary things well against an elite opponent, which he said starts with coaching. He acknowledged that the Seahawks' pressure and disguises, including Mike Macdonald-style looks, made the passing game stall when Jacoby Brissett was under pressure, and he said the tape needs review. On the Seattle receiver, he called Jaxon Smith-Njigba a dang good receiver and said the scheme and execution both fell short, especially in covering him. On personnel, he said the 13-personnel package limited the number of receivers on the field, which explained some of the snap and target distribution. He said Trey McBride had some targets but that the team shouldn't read too much into the passing numbers because the offense didn't throw well. He said Max Melton has a foot injury and Will Johnson a neck injury, with more information coming the next day, and said both initially told him they were fine. He stressed the team can't let the loss carry into next week, which will be against a healthy, rolling opponent he didn't name.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a foot injury; LaFleur said more information would come the next day.
Left the game with a neck injury; LaFleur said he initially said he was fine, with more information to come.

signals.claim: Passing offense struggled when Brissett was pressured; the staff will adjust protection or the pressure plan and review the tape.
signals.note: Pressure-heavy defenses limited the passing game, which suppresses Brissett's upside until the fix shows up.

signals.quote: Obviously Trey had some, but I wouldn't look into too much

topics.detail: The team led 7-7 at halftime but lost after a second-half collapse of three-and-outs and six-and-outs, with the defense holding until the final 20 minutes. LaFleur said execution and coaching were the problems, not wholesale changes.

Heavy use of 13 personnel limited the number of receivers on the field. The coach referenced Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr. in those packages, but who was on the field for how many snaps was not clearly confirmed.
LaFleur said next week's opponent is rolling and healthy, and the team cannot let the Seattle loss carry over.

title: Kevin Stefanski reflects on Atlanta Falcons vs Carolina Panthers matchup | Press Conference
headline: Falcons' QB picture stays unsettled: Penix has no clear timeline, and Cooper Rush's Week 3 status is undecided after a turnover-heavy loss to Carolina.
summary: Stefanski said he was extremely disappointed by the loss to Carolina, which began badly and got away from the team in the second half. He stressed that turnovers decided the game, with Atlanta giving the ball away repeatedly and forcing none, and he called the first-play turnover correctable. He said the team's performance was not close to its standard and that the fault was shared across the roster, not one position. On Michael Penix Jr., he said he had no update and that Penix is continuing to progress, but he would not say what the plan is for this week. He praised Cooper Rush's effort but would not discuss his confidence in Rush or Jack Strand, and he declined to say whether Rush's back was a factor. Asked whether Rush would start Week 3 if Penix or Tua Tagovailoa is unavailable, he said it was not fair to address that yet. He also said he takes responsibility for every call, and he credited Carolina for a late fourth-and-one play. Thursday night's game is next, and he wants the team to move on quickly.

topics.detail: The Falcons lost to Carolina in Week 2. They started poorly, turned the ball over repeatedly, and forced no takeaways. The team also had no red-zone trips in the first two games, which Stefanski attributed to turnovers and turnovers on downs.

title: Dave Canales evaluates Week 2 win over Falcons
headline: Bryce Young and Xavier Legette look strong, Devin Lloyd had a dominant game, and Jonathon Brooks is day-to-day with a re-aggravated groin.
summary: Dave Canales praised the complementary win, crediting the defense with four takeaways and two fourth-down stops that gave the offense short fields. He said the offense left points in the red zone and lost roughly 60 to 70 rushing yards to penalties, which the staff wants to fix. Special teams flipped field position, with Jalen Coker's punt returns praised and the coverage unit called fast and physical. Canales said Xavier Legette's big play was the momentum shift and that Legette had his best practice week of Canales's tenure. He called Devin Lloyd's performance (two interceptions, a sack, a batted pass, eight tackles) one of the most dominant linebacker games he has seen in 17 years. On the offense, he said Bryce Young is taking ownership of the system, fine-tuning routes and timing with receivers. Canales said Darren Waller's veteran decisiveness and understanding of leverage, built through work with Young, is driving his red-zone production. On injuries, Jonathon Brooks re-aggravated his groin and is day-to-day, Mitchell Evans was cleared after cramping, Trevis Gipson was fine, and a rib/abdominal injury to a young defensive lineman (Nick) is being evaluated. A shoulder injury to Claude Cherilus kept him out of the game.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Week 2 Victory Over Texans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Burrow took hits but coach says he's fine, and Ja'Marr Chase's receiving TD doesn't signal a target shift for Cincinnati.
summary: Zac Taylor praised the complete team effort in Cincinnati's road win over Houston, highlighting the defense's early pressure, Dexter Lawrence's fourth-and-one stop, and the special teams' field position work. He said the offense couldn't capitalize early and that Houston's defensive line made the game difficult. On Ja'Marr Chase's touchdown catch, Taylor said the team doesn't worry about targets, that Chase was a positive captain throughout, and that his big games will come. Taylor credited Drew Sample as a leader and blocker who doesn't get enough credit. On Joe Burrow, Taylor said he stood in against pressure, got his legs back, and made big throws, and that a hit he took didn't concern him based on recent feedback. Taylor said the run defense let the team play more freely and that the second half was cleaner. He also said the offense will need to clean up some things.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Buccaneers: September 20th, 2026
headline: Watson's Week 2 starting status vs. Carolina is unresolved: Monken heaped praise on him but dodged the starter question.
summary: Monken was proud of the team's second-half comeback in the 23-19 win over Tampa Bay and called it a players' win, while acknowledging the first half was poor. He said the team had used the delay to hydrate, fuel, and keep the players loose, and he praised the defense for closing it out. He gave Deshaun Watson major credit, saying he played very well in the second half despite the run game struggling, and he took responsibility for the offensive scheme and play-calling. When asked directly whether Watson will start at home against Carolina, Monken refused to answer and said he would just enjoy the win. Monken said the first-half problems included lost-yardage plays, penalties, and failed conversions, which he blamed on both players and coaching. He said Denzel Boston was not a surprise, but that the team needed to get him the ball more. He credited defensive coordinator Rudy and his staff for the defensive turnaround after the prior week's poor performance. The team now turns its attention to Carolina.

signals.claim: Coach did not confirm Watson will start at home against Carolina; the question was deflected.
signals.note: Starter status is the key fantasy question for Watson's next start, and Monken offered no clarity despite heavy praise.
signals.quote: I'm just going to leave it there.

signals.note: A stated desire for more targets for Boston suggests a possible increase in his passing-game role, though it was not a firm promise.
signals.quote: Other than we needed him to get the ball more.

topics.detail: Monken said the offense lacked a running game, which made it hard to control the line of scrimmage, and he took responsibility for the schematic and play-calling side. The team plans to run the ball better, and the offense leaned on quick throws to get the ball out of Watson's hands against Tampa Bay's pressure.

The defense was credited for a strong second-half performance after a poor prior week, and Monken praised defensive coordinator Rudy and the staff. He said the unit was the group he wanted to close out the win.
The team's next game is a home matchup against the Carolina Panthers. Monken did not give an update on injuries or personnel for that game.

He also said the news on the player transcribed as Zach Thomas doesn't look good and that the player could be out for a long time. He praised the team's resiliency after falling behind by ten in the fourth quarter, highlighting the run defense, pressure on the quarterback, and a special teams unit he called one of the best in the league. On the offensive line, he said several backups stepped up, including Anthony Belton and Jager Burton, and that at one point the team was down to four healthy linemen while Jacob Monk was evaluated. He credited Jonathan Gannon for an aggressive defensive game plan and called him an elite coordinator. LaFleur acknowledged the team put itself in too many bad situations, including negative runs and penalties, and said the 14 penalties need to be cleaned up, especially false starts and offside calls. He said Kaleb Johnson showed good outside zone running and is getting more comfortable with the offense, so he will likely earn more opportunities. He also praised Lukas Van Ness as a player coming into his own and said he can be very impactful. LaFleur declined to address a question about trading for linemen or running backs.

He defended Drake Maye's interception decision as something to review on tape, said the team must stay aggressive, and said he trusts Maye's decisions. title: Kellen Moore reacts to Saints' Win against Ravens | Saints-Ravens Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 2
headline: Tyler Shough's steady play and Juwan Johnson's catch-and-run stood out, while Kelvin Banks (ankle) is a short-term injury watch to check Monday.
summary: Kellen Moore credited the Saints' resiliency in a close win over Baltimore, saying the offense stalled for long stretches with field goals and a bad three-and-out before a key drive got it going. He said the defense kept battling, especially on a long third-quarter drive that ended in a field goal, and that the team's close connection is what keeps players focused through tough moments. On the late fourth-down call and goal-line plays, he defended the aggressiveness, said the false start hurt the goal-line situation, and said the officials gave no explanation on a third-down review. He praised the defensive front and linebackers against Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry and said Tyler Shough was steady, made good decisions, and delivered in the late stretch. Moore said Juwan Johnson's catch-and-run on the third-and-eight was a big play, and that early-game struggles with negative early downs need cleanup. He said Kelvin Banks has an ankle injury that will be re-evaluated the next day, and that Kevin Austin Jr. stepped in well for him. On inactives, he said it was a numbers decision at tight end and running back, with Johnson having been sick and Oscar Delp returning, and said Kendre Miller will play a lot of football.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (9/20) | Week 2
headline: Jets lost in overtime; Glenn defended the decision to take the ball first and trusts Geno Smith, but injury updates on Mason Taylor and David Onyemata are pending midweek.
summary: Glenn said he was highly upset with the loss and listed several areas to fix, including penalties (13 on his team, 14 on the opponent), special teams, failing to establish the run, and defensive breakdowns that let the opponent drive and score. He said the loss would not define the team but called it unacceptable and said the team must go on the road next week against a familiar opponent. He defended choosing to receive the ball first in overtime, arguing that controlling the clock and putting pressure on the other team was the plan, though it did not work out. He said he had a lot of trust in the run game on the fourth-down call at midfield, though he said he would have to review the tape to explain it, and he defended the field goal decision as taking points. He said he trusts Geno Smith, who was not at his best, and that the team should have run the ball on the early overtime drop-backs. He rejected the idea that the team lacked competitive stamina, saying the players competed hard all game. He also said he didn't consider a timeout on the late third-down stop because a punt would have pinned the opponent deep. On injuries, he listed ankle, quad, groin, knee and thumb issues for several players and promised updates later in the week.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 20, 2026
headline: Eagles' OT win over Tennessee: Jalen Hurts praised for leading the late drive, Darius Cooper praised for his role, and Landon Dickerson left the game with no clear timeline.
summary: Sirianni called the 24-20 overtime win a strong organizational effort, with attention to detail across the building, and said the team dug deep in the heat. He explained the decision to shift the offensive line configuration, saying it gave the team its best chance to win, and said it could carry forward but wasn't committing to that. He praised Jalen Hurts as the captain and an example of composure, and said Hurts' habits showed up during the late drive. On the late touchdown drive, Sirianni said the team used early timeouts and an aggressive approach, and credited the explosive plays, the calls, and the protection. He wasn't satisfied with the ground game, said the team needs to run more efficiently, and said the film would be reviewed. He credited Darius Cooper for dirty work, a special teams tackle, and accepting his role. Sirianni said Landon Dickerson left the game and that backups stepped in, and he did not address the status of Saquon Barkley or Dallas Goedert. He said the players have Monday off and return to work Tuesday.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Patriots
headline: McCarthy blames himself for a sloppy offense, says game-plan volume will be cut, and hints at more work for Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson while Michael Pittman's role is in question.
summary: McCarthy said the offense was not good enough and took responsibility, saying the detail and coaching start with him as the play caller. He described the run game as herky-jerky, protections as unclean against expected pressure, and communication breakdowns that cost big-play chances, especially in the first half. He said the offense's volume will be reduced until it executes cleanly, which he called his fault for not catching it earlier in the week. He praised Aaron Rodgers as able to handle any volume but said the team needs to give him better platforms and more downfield opportunities. He credited the defense with holding New England to 13 points and called special teams a wash that he still needs to review. On Michael Pittman, he said the veteran had been fighting through injuries and was finding rhythm with Rodgers, but that the lower production creates opportunities for others, and he will look at Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson. He had no update on Rico Dowdle's injury because he had not been to the training room.

injuries.detail: Asked for an update on his injury; McCarthy said he had no update because he had not been in the training room.

McCarthy said the defense played well enough to win, holding the Patriots to 13 points, while special teams was a wash that he needs to review.
McCarthy said the officiating crew called the game tight and the team had a couple of big penalties that need to be cleaned up.

title: Todd Bowles on Result of Browns vs. Bucs | Press Conference
headline: Bowles blames offensive penalties and second-half missed tackles for the loss, and says Godwin and Egbuka were doubled early.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs look out of sync because of too many offensive penalties and too many second-half missed tackles on defense. He told the team nobody is coming to save them and that they must correct their own mistakes quickly. He called this adversity they have faced before, though it is the first such situation at the start of this season. On the offense, he said the team needs a better early ground game and probably some quicker passes. He acknowledged that the screen game to running backs was something Cleveland had shown on film, but he did not elaborate on its success. On defense, he said the Browns' Watson-led second half came from missed tackles and a collision that let a runner score. He said he thought the pass rush was better than the prior week but still needs work. Bowles said the multi-hour weather delay affected both teams equally and was not an excuse.
